A rope is attached at one end of the beam. The rope is at an angle of 60 to the vertical and
exerts a force F, in newtons, on the beam.
What is the moment, in N m, of the force F about the point S?
A
1.1F
B
1.3F
C
1.9F
D
2.2F

hints: Notice the pivot S is $0.30 \text{ m}$ from end Q, while P is $2.5 \text{ m}$ from Q, so find the distance PS first.
The rope force $F$ is $60^{\circ}$ to the vertical, so resolve it into vertical $F\cos 60^{\circ}$ and horizontal $F\sin 60^{\circ}$ components.
Only the vertical component has a perpendicular distance from S because the horizontal component acts along the line of the beam, so multiply the correct component by PS.
walkthrough: Find the distance from the line of the force to the pivot. $PS = 2.5 - 0.30 = 2.2 \text{ m}$ to the left of S.
Resolve $F$ which is $60^{\circ}$ to the vertical. Vertical component upward is $F_{v} = F\cos 60^{\circ}$ and horizontal component to the left is $F_{h} = F\sin 60^{\circ}$.
Decide which component gives a moment about S. The horizontal component acts at beam level with zero perpendicular distance, so its moment about S is zero.
The vertical component is perpendicular to the horizontal beam, so its moment is force times distance: $\text{moment} = F_{v} \times PS$.
Substitute values: $\text{moment} = F\cos 60^{\circ} \times 2.2 = F \times 0.5 \times 2.2 = 1.1F$ with unit $\text{N m}$.

A.explanation: Moment is $2.2 \times F\cos 60^{\circ} = 1.1F$ in $\text{N m}$, the vertical component times distance PS.

B.explanation: Uses the full $2.5 \text{ m}$ length from P to Q instead of the $2.2 \text{ m}$ distance from P to S, giving $2.5F\cos 60^{\circ} \approx 1.3F$.

D.explanation: Uses the full force $F$ times $2.2 \text{ m}$ with no resolution for the $60^{\circ}$ angle, giving $2.2F$.
